description: Students start secondary science by asking what science is and how scientists know what they know. They learn their way around the lab and its equipment, the safety rules that keep everyone safe, and the steps of a scientific investigation. Three hands-on labs build the measuring skills every later unit depends on: reading balances, measuring cylinders, thermometers and timers precisely and recording results in tables.
notes: Listed as S.S.S on the 2027 scope and sequence and the work tracker.
**No site unit or slide decks exist for this unit yet**, so explicit instruction and activity sheet links are placeholders.
The measuring skills here are assessed later, inside the Particle Model experiments and CAT — this unit has no CAT of its own.

print.text: Science Skills and Safety workbook {{PH:workbook link}}

achievement.text: Develop questions and predictions; plan safe investigations, identifying risks; select equipment and use it to collect precise data; organise data in tables; communicate findings using scientific vocabulary.
Explain how scientific knowledge is built from evidence and can change when new evidence appears.

descriptors.text: Scientific knowledge, including models and theories, can change in light of new evidence
Develop investigable questions, reasoned predictions and hypotheses
Plan and conduct safe, reproducible investigations, identifying variables, risks and ethical considerations
Select and use equipment to generate and record precise data
Organise data in tables, graphs and models
Communicate ideas and findings using suitable formats and scientific vocabulary

prepare: Opening task: what does a scientist do? Draw one — then compare with real scientists.
Check primary-school measuring: rulers, scales and thermometers.
review: Lab-equipment naming quiz; safety rules quiz before the first hands-on lab.
Measuring results tables checked each lab.
diff: Labelled equipment photo cards; a scale-reading guide with worked examples; results tables with a red first row.
Safety rules as a picture checklist.
extension: Calculate the uncertainty (± half the smallest division) of each instrument.
Design a fair test of your own question using the method steps.

lessons.title: What is science?
li: Describe what science is and how scientific knowledge is built from evidence.
Tell an observation from an inference.
Write a question that can be investigated.
sc: I can give an example of an observation and an inference, and turn a curious question into one I can test.
review: Exit question: one observation and one inference about a mystery object

lessons.title: Lab: exploring the lab
li: Name and draw common lab equipment and say what each is used for.
sc: I can name ten pieces of equipment, draw three as scientific diagrams, and point out the safety equipment.

prac.name: Exploring the lab — equipment stations and a safety-equipment hunt
prac.si: Select the right equipment for a task and draw it as a scientific diagram (VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Identify hazards in the lab and the equipment that controls them (VC2S8I02).

lessons.title: Lab: measuring weights and volumes
li: Read an electronic balance and a measuring cylinder precisely.
sc: I can read a measuring cylinder at eye level from the bottom of the meniscus and record mass and volume with units.
explicit: Worked examples: reading scales, the meniscus, units

prac.name: Measuring mass and volume — stations with balances, measuring cylinders and beakers
prac.si: Use equipment to collect precise measurements and record them in a table with units (VC2S8I03, VC2S8I04).
prac.su: Explain the difference between mass and volume.

review: Results table checked against the teacher’s values

lessons.title: The scientific method
li: Describe the steps of a scientific investigation: question, hypothesis, method, results, conclusion.
Identify independent, dependent and controlled variables in a fair test.
Write a hypothesis as “If … then … because …”.
sc: I can identify the three kinds of variable in an experiment and write a hypothesis.
review: Exit question: the variables in a paper-helicopter drop

lessons.title: Safety
li: Follow the lab safety rules and explain why each one matters.
Identify hazards and risks, and how to control them, in a simple risk assessment.
Light and use a Bunsen burner safely.
sc: I can complete a risk assessment for a simple experiment and pass the safety quiz.
guided: Safety contract signed and glued in
review: Safety quiz — required before the next hands-on lab

lessons.title: Lab: measuring temperature and time
li: Read a thermometer and a stopwatch precisely, and record readings over time.
sc: I can measure the temperature of water as it heats every minute and record it in a table.
explicit: Worked examples: reading a thermometer, timing intervals

prac.name: Measuring temperature and time — heating water with a Bunsen burner, temperature every minute
prac.si: Use equipment safely to record temperature at regular time intervals in a table (VC2S8I02, VC2S8I03, VC2S8I04).
prac.su: Describe how the temperature of water changes as it is heated.
prac.risk: {{PH:RiskAssess link — heating water with a Bunsen burner}}

review: Results table checked; this data is reused for the first line graph in the Particle Model
